no_overclaim_note: This wave's pytest file is a TEST/EVIDENCE artifact only. No production code (completion_inbox.py, core.py, server.py) was changed. Every item below is a real, test-confirmed gap between the B277/B278 owner-notification envelope design and what the current read-only tool layer actually returns -- none of them are implemented by this task.

blockers.description: completion_inbox._fetch_full_cards never inspects the LIST subcommand's returncode -- only stdout is parsed. A LIST-call read-source failure (e.g. sqlite lock, taskctl crash) with empty stdout is indistinguishable from a genuinely empty queue: zero rows, zero fetch_errors, no signal to the owner.
blockers.proposed_fix: In completion_inbox._fetch_full_cards, check list_result.get('returncode') before parsing stdout; on non-zero, append a fetch_errors entry tagged {"scope": "list", "status": cstatus, "error": stderr} instead of silently treating it as zero rows.

blockers.description: No server.py tool, no completion_inbox.py facet, and no exception-handling wrapper exists anywhere for a read-source failure to degrade to a bounded result instead of an uncaught exception (test_scenario_tool_error_current_raises_uncaught proves the raise-through today).
blockers.proposed_fix: Wrap the eventual aiworkhub_completion_inbox_delta implementation's core.run_taskctl calls in a try/except that returns {"ok": false, "error_kind": "read_source_failure", "error_message": str(exc)} per B278's tool_error expected_payload shape, never letting the exception cross the MCP tool boundary.

blockers.description: core.usage_report() only exposes AITools/taskctl.py::cmd_usage_report's human-readable TEXT report. There is no structured per-task usage event (usage_input_tokens/usage_output_tokens/cost_usd) the way B278's scenario_usage expects. A per-card usage_summary dict DOES exist on cards returned by show_task (per cmd_usage_report's own source, card.get('usage_summary')), so a structured usage facet is derivable without a new taskctl subcommand -- it just is not exposed by any current core.py/completion_inbox.py function.
blockers.proposed_fix: Add a core.py helper (e.g. usage_records(topic=...)) that calls list_tasks/show_task (already-read-only) and extracts card['usage_summary'] directly, producing the structured per-task payload B278 expects, instead of parsing cmd_usage_report's text output.

blockers.evidence: test_scenario_duplicate_runner (PASS, using a code-compatible fixture instead of B278's literal one)
blockers.description: B278's duplicate_runner fixture models TWO DIFFERENT runners colliding on one task_id (conflicting_runner_a vs conflicting_runner_b). The real completion_inbox facet (runner_mismatch_warnings, backed by _runner_task_batch_mismatch) only checks a SINGLE card's own runner against its OWN task_id's batch token -- a self-consistency check, not a cross-runner collision detector. The actual cross-runner collision detector is core.collision_guard()/core._extract_collision_report (different field shape entirely: file/conflicting_tasks), untouched by this task's fixtures beyond being named here.
blockers.proposed_fix: Before aiworkhub_completion_inbox_delta claims to emit a duplicate_runner event, decide explicitly whether it is sourced from _runner_task_batch_mismatch (self-consistency) or collision_guard (cross-runner file collision) -- they are not interchangeable, and B278's fixture shape only matches neither cleanly today.

blockers.description: Several facet field names differ from the B277/B278 canonical envelope: stale_hours vs hours_since_activity, last_activity_at vs last_recorded_at (plus an extra lifecycle_state key on latest_validation_facts), runner_task_batch_mismatch=None vs JSON false.
blockers.proposed_fix: A thin adapter layer (not a rewrite of completion_inbox.py) should remap these field names when/if aiworkhub_completion_inbox_delta is built, so the delta tool's payloads match the frozen B277 envelope schema exactly while completion_inbox.py itself keeps its current field names for backward compatibility with existing B275/B276 consumers.
